scenes.title: Object Storage Fundamentals
scenes.narration: Object storage keeps files as objects inside buckets, offering nearly unlimited, durable, and cheap storage that underpins almost every cloud data lake.

scenes.title: What Makes It Special
bullets: Objects are stored in a flat namespace with a key, not a traditional folder tree.
It scales to virtually unlimited capacity and offers extremely high durability, often eleven nines.
It is inexpensive and accessible over HTTP, making it ideal for storing raw data at scale.
scenes.narration: Unlike a file system, object storage uses a flat namespace where each object has a unique key. It scales without practical limits and is engineered for eleven nines of durability, meaning data loss is exceedingly rare. Low cost and simple HTTP access make it the natural home for raw data lakes.

scenes.title: Object Storage vs. File System
scenes.narration: A file system nests folders and is bound to a specific machine's disk. Object storage instead uses flat keys, is reached over an API, and scales without the size ceiling of a physical disk. The slash-separated key just simulates folders for human convenience.

scenes.title: Anatomy of an Object
scenes.narration: Every object lives inside a bucket, identified by a key that looks like a path. The value is the raw file content, and metadata carries details like content type and custom tags. Understanding these four parts demystifies how the cloud stores your data.

scenes.title: Storage Across Providers
scenes.code:
# AWS S3
aws s3 cp data.csv s3://my-bucket/raw/data.csv

# Google Cloud Storage
gsutil cp data.csv gs://my-bucket/raw/data.csv

# Azure Data Lake Storage
az storage blob upload -f data.csv -c raw --account-name myacct
scenes.narration: Each provider ships a command-line tool that speaks to its object store. On AWS you use the s3 command, on Google the gsutil tool, and on Azure the az storage commands. Notice how the URLs differ by scheme but the idea of copying a file into a bucket is identical everywhere.

scenes.text: Object storage is the durable, cheap, and infinitely scalable foundation of the cloud data lake — master buckets and keys and everything else builds on top.
scenes.narration: Object storage is the bedrock of modern data lakes because it is durable, cheap, and endlessly scalable. Once buckets and keys feel natural, the rest of cloud data engineering stacks neatly on top.
